clue.text: Forbid people standing outside damaged arena in weak state

indicators.note: standing outside says the forbid-and-people pair goes around the reworked arena letters

parts.note: to forbid is to ban
the people at large are the public

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of arena are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A banned crowd hangs about outside a wrecked stadium while the country falters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns the arena into ANARE; 'standing outside' has the two outer words flank it. 'people' looks like the subject of the surface, but it gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana republic is a politically unstable small country, a weak state dependent on one export.

clue.text: Puzzling magnetic variation around island

indicators.note: around says the varied letters wrap round the island's letter
variation signals that the letters of magnetic are varied into a new order

explanation.surface: A compass needle behaves strangely near an island, baffling navigators.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MAGNETIC, rearranged under 'variation', go around I to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enigmatic is mysterious and hard to fathom, which is what puzzling means.

clue.text: Have one's home days at the beginning of spring

indicators.note: at the beginning of places the days abbreviation in front of the spring word

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for days, as on calendars
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone moves house in the first days of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or reside there, i.e. to have your home there.

clue.text: Composite platform, the fourth for Marylebone

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform

indicators.note: the fourth for points to the fourth letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A railway platform number at Marylebone station in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composite' is a botanical noun: the composites are the daisy family (Compositae). 'Marylebone' is a London station, which helps the railway-platform picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call members of the aster family composites, and the common lawn flower is the classic example.

clue.text: Play some specific contestants

definitions.meaning: a stage comedy by Sheridan, first staged in 1775
particular competitors, the definite article plus a word for opponents

explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's comedy has this title, and the phrase also literally names a particular set of competitors.

clue.text: Futile having a weapon to the left used by right-winger

indicators.note: to the left means the weapon word is written leftwards, i.e. backwards in an across entry

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a Tory is a British Conservative, a right-winger

explanation.surface: A pointless weapon aimed leftwards by a man of the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' reverses GUN to NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or effect, a formal synonym for futile.

clue.text: Nearly all stand around at stable

indicators.note: around says the shortened stand word goes round the little word at
nearly all means the final letter of the stand word is dropped

parts.note: to stick something is to stand or tolerate it, as in can't stick it

explanation.surface: Horses nearly all stand around at the stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' makes STIC, and 'around' wraps it round AT. 'stable' is the adjective meaning steady, not the horses' building, and 'stand' means tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means unchanging and fixed, so it is a synonym for stable as an adjective.

clue.text: Needle person in front of relations

indicators.note: in front of puts the person word before the relations word

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: A person with a needle stands before their family.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a blunt thick needle used for threading tape or elastic.

clue.text: Nut to fasten part of engine

parts.note: a nut is a crank, an eccentric person
to pin is to fasten

explanation.surface: A mechanic uses a nut to fasten part of an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' suggests the hardware beside the engine, but it is an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A crankpin is the pin on a crankshaft that connects it to the connecting rod.

clue.text: No quality in fast food eats accepted by sailors

indicators.note: accepted by means the eating word is taken inside the sailors word

parts.note: tars are sailors in crossword convention
someone who eats food dines

explanation.surface: Sailors take on fast food that has no quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' looks like one phrase, but 'fast' ends the definition: the quality of not being quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is slowness or lateness, the very quality that being quick lacks.

clue.text: Young bear nearly frozen — like solid

parts.note: a cub is a young bear

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the frozen word is dropped

parts.note: icy means frozen

explanation.surface: A bear cub is almost frozen solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ICY to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic describes a three-dimensional shape like the solid figure a cube, so it means like a solid.

clue.text: Selfie with one stripped? Charming

indicators.note: stripped means both words lose their outer letters, leaving only the insides

explanation.surface: Someone poses for a selfie with a stripper, and finds it charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' leaves ELFI from SELFIE and N from ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means delicately pretty and charming, like an elf.

clue.text: A time cutting to grind round fruit from Mexico

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cutting says the a-and-time letters slice into the grind word

parts.note: to mill is to grind
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A time-consuming effort to grind a round Mexican fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' gives MATILL. The surface's 'A time' reads as a phrase, but the two words split into separate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small green husked fruit used in Mexican cooking, such as salsa verde.

clue.text: He needs the manly ones about the place for rowing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the following words are moved around

explanation.surface: He needs strong rowers about the place for a boat race.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands as written; THE MANLY ONES rearranged under 'about' make the rest. The town is on the Thames in Oxfordshire and hosts the famous Henley Royal Regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: This Thames-side town hosts the world-famous Henley Royal Regatta, so it is a celebrated rowing venue.

clue.text: Routine where one's reportedly mated with goat?

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: bred and butter, i.e. a creature bred with a butter, a goat being something that butts

explanation.surface: A farmer's routine consists of mating animals with a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: A goat is a 'butter' because it butts; 'mated with' it is 'bred and butter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter work is the basic everyday routine that provides one's living.

clue.text: Tacking when yachting — with 180 degree heading change

indicators.note: a 180 degree change of heading turns south into north, so the S is replaced by N

parts.note: yachting is sailing

explanation.surface: A yacht tacks by swinging its heading through 180 degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' is the first letter: the S of SAILING, South, turns 180 degrees to N, North. 'Tacking' means fixing with tacks, not the sailing manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking something down means fastening it with small nails, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: One wanting to protect area game has in reserve

parts.note: nim is a game of taking objects from heaps
something put by is kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A protector of the area keeps a game in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: NIMBY stands for 'not in my back yard': someone who opposes development near home.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimby objects to developments in their own locality, wanting to keep the neighbourhood unchanged.

clue.text: Rubbish located by old railway turning

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense
at means located in a place

explanation.surface: Rubbish has piled up beside an old railway turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory means rotating or causing rotation, so it describes something turning.

clue.text: A lot of money left unseen in pocket opening

indicators.note: unseen means the left letter disappears from the word for the opening

parts.note: a placket is a slit in a garment, often giving access to a pocket

explanation.surface: A big wad of cash lies hidden in a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: PLACKET loses L under 'unseen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Packet is British slang for a large sum of money, as in costing a packet.

clue.text: China's pursuing offensive game

indicators.note: pursuing puts the china word after the offensive word

parts.note: bad can mean offensive, as in bad language
Minton is a famous English porcelain maker, so its name stands for china

explanation.surface: China is chasing an aggressive game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain, MINTON being the English maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played over a net with a shuttlecock.

clue.text: Lax one succeeding when keeping account

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: keeping means the succeeding word holds the account abbreviation inside it

parts.note: next means succeeding, following on

explanation.surface: A careless person succeeds while handling the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise or loose, so lax in the sense of lacking rigour.

clue.text: Knowing where one stands with group of students on reasoning

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a class is a group of students
conscious means aware and capable of thought, reasoning

explanation.surface: Someone learns their place through a class of students reasoning together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being class-conscious means being aware of one's social rank, knowing where one stands socially.

clue.text: New Zealand bird using keys outside current teaching's style

parts.note: the tui is a New Zealand honeyeater

indicators.note: outside means the keys word wraps round the current symbol

parts.note: tonal music is written using keys
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A New Zealand bird plays the keys outside an electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives TIONAL. 'keys' suggests a piano, but tonal music is music organised in keys; the tui is a native honeyeater.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuitional means relating to tuition, so it describes something in the manner of teaching.

clue.text: First-year student is somewhat forceful and cool to staff

parts.note: a fresh wind is fairly strong and cool
to man is to staff

explanation.surface: A new student is a bit pushy and keeps a cool head with staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the verb, as in staffing a desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshman is a student in the first year at college or university.

clue.text: French composer of "Fleur du mal"?

indicators.note: mal is French for badly, so the preceding words are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Who wrote 'Les Fleurs du mal'? Baudelaire's poems seem to name a French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Duruflé (1902-86) was a French organist and composer. The quotation looks like the title of Baudelaire's poems, but 'mal' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Duruflé was a French composer and organist, best known for his Requiem.

clue.text: Ripping up album — bland stuff

indicators.note: ripping tears the letters apart so they can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone tears up a dull album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is fodder, not part of 'Ripping up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pabulum is insipid intellectual fare, bland material lacking substance.

clue.text: Picket stuck without food on way in

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the remaining letter on top of the way-in word
without means the food word is taken out of the stuck word

parts.note: tuck is British schoolchildren's slang for food
an entry is a way in

explanation.surface: A striker on the picket line is stuck at the entrance without food.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking TUCK from STUCK leaves S. 'Picket' is a guard, not a striker.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket is a soldier or small group posted on guard, the same role as a sentry.

clue.text: Lash Conservative over hospital problem being concealed

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the Conservative letter above the hospital letter

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip, a lash

explanation.surface: A Conservative lashes out over a hospital scandal being covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden snag or drawback, as in what's the catch.
